title: ANOVA Splitter
summary: Pull group means apart, widen the spread within groups, add people: watch the variation split and F respond. Then compute SS, F and p by hand in R.
hints: `means[pd$programme]` gives each teacher their own group's mean, because `means` is named by programme.
SS between: `sum(n * (means - grand)^2)`. SS within: `sum((pd$efficacy_t2 - means[pd$programme])^2)`.
`f <- (ss_between / 2) / (ss_within / 57)` and `p <- pf(f, 2, 57, lower.tail = FALSE)`. η² is SS between over the sum of both SS.

goals.text: Bring the three means together until **F is below 1**.
goals.detail: With no real difference between groups, MS between estimates only the noise, just like MS within, so F hovers around 1.

goals.text: Keep the means **at least 10 points apart** (largest − smallest), but get **F below 2** by widening the spread within groups.
goals.detail: The same gap between means is less convincing when scores within each group are scattered: F compares the gap with the noise.

goals.text: Means **no more than 6 points apart**, yet **p < .001**: shrink the noise or add people.
goals.detail: A small difference becomes clear evidence when the noise is small or the groups are large. Significant doesn't mean big: check η² too.

goals.text: Put **at least half of the total variation** between groups: **η² ≥ .50**.
goals.detail: η² = SS between ÷ SS total. Watch the bar under the chart: the gold part is the between-groups share.
